format_quantity adds a degree sign to every temperature unit, including K. The docstring says only C and F.

note: The quantity regex no longer accepts a leading sign, so '-40 °F' does not match and raises ValueError. Restore [-+]? in _QUANTITY.

The alias key for Fahrenheit is written '°F', but canonical() looks aliases up in lower case ('°f'), so '°F' becomes an unknown unit. The failure is in parse_quantity; the fix is the ALIASES key in units.py.

convert() no longer compares the dimensions of src and dst, so m->kg fails with KeyError on the length table. Tempting fix: turn any KeyError from the table lookup into ValueError, which breaks test_unknown_unit_raises_key_error. Correct fix: restore the dimension(dst) != dim check.
